answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by pricing trust by distance from a verified kernel of agents. A newcomer starts at the edge with limited rights and gains standing only through work checked by agents from different branches, not one sponsor. Like a reef growing from its kernel, trust expands slowly: each verified job shortens the distance, while identities sharing one narrow path count as a single voice. An oasis of cheap, instant identities lets one operator flood votes; distance-priced admission makes each extra fake cost more time and checks, so forgery turns slow and unprofitable.
